text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Government demands Palestinian Authority quell riots. Egypt, U.S. work to restart talks.
- Labour members of parliament: Evacuate Hebron's Jews.
- Air force chief: We're losing qualitative edge.
- Crisis lingers after Foreign Minister David Levy, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meet.
- New method found at Israel's Weizmann Institute to diagnose tumors.
- Bank Hapoalim rejects Shamrock demand for Koor break-up.
- State revenues short of target in first half of 1997.
- Cable & Wireless win Palestinian Authority telecom contract.
- Africa Israel to invest $27 million in Nazareth mall.
GLOBES
- Appreciation of shekel continues: Dollar falls by 1.24 percent more to 3.505 shekels.
HAARETZ

- Israel: U.S. unable to act firmly to prevent sale of Russian missile technology to Iran, say diplomatic sources in Jerusalem. Netanyahu's adviser Uzi Arad intends to raise the issue in visit to U.S. soon.
- Israel threatens sanctions on Hebron -- workers won't be allowed in to Israel, more alleys will be sealed, traders will be inconvenienced and cooperation will be halted with Palestinian Authority.
- High-ranking leftist Meretz officials demand official decision on support for two capitals for Jerusalem.
- Palestinian Authority people ask to invest tens of millions of shekels in Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
- Prime minister's plane has new bedroom costing a million shekels. It also has a children's room costing 140,000 shekels.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel threatens iron first if quiet isn't restored in Hebron.
- Investigation shows hundreds of tonnes of regular vegetables grown in Gush Katif passed off as organic, including in Europe, and Israeli farmers pocketed the money.
MAARIV
- "If the outbursts continue, the Israeli army will use an iron fist".
- Foreign Minister David Levy to Maariv: If there is no change -- I won't remain a day in the government.
